counterfactual_missing_items: He denied trauma, fever, steroid or other drug intake, and infections.
On examination he was non-obese (65 kg, 167 cm; BMI 23.3 kg/m2) with no signs of Cushing syndrome or endocrinopathy.
Routine hematological and biochemical tests and cerebrospinal fluid analysis were normal.
decisive_items: a posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7, with a maximum thickness of 10 mm that was homogeneously hyperintense on both T1-weighted and T2-weighted sequences, suggestive of fat
ascending spastic weakness of the lower limbs
graded sensory loss below the D10 level
response.rationale: R1 is the only candidate anchored to the diagnostic MRI finding of posterior epidural fat, which directly identifies spinal epidural lipomatosis. R3 and C1 describe the downstream spinal cord compression syndrome but do not identify the underlying epidural fat or provide etiologic specificity. C1 is a redundant append-only completion of R3, adding only an inferred thoracic modifier from the same sensory-level span.

rejected.why: Append-only completion of R3; its sole raw span duplicates R3's sensory-level evidence and the thoracic modifier is inferred rather than a distinct diagnostic entity.
